name: Exploring efficiently and avoiding costly mistakes
gist: Finding smart ways to explore unknown situations without wasting time, and understanding how much the agent could regret a bad decision so we know when to stop exploring.
explain: In any learning problem, there is a core tension: do you try new things and risk failure, or stick with what you know works? Try the new restaurant — it might be great, or it might ruin dinner. Test a new ad campaign — it could double sales, or it could flop. A robot should try new grasping strategies — to handle new shapes — but not so many times that it breaks things. This is the exploration-exploitation trade-off. Learning fast means exploring smart: try things where success is likely, not random shots in the dark.

The hard part is measuring how bad a wrong choice could be. If the robot tried one action and got a poor outcome, how much should it regret that choice? Maybe the outcome was unlucky, or maybe the action is actually terrible. Researchers measure regret — the cost of not knowing the optimal action — to decide when to stop exploring and commit. If the possible regret of exploring is high (like in a medical setting where mistakes harm patients), explore less. If regret is low (like in simulations), explore more. Papers in this area work on bandit algorithms — methods for learning which choice is best when you have limited tries and need to balance trying new things against the cost of mistakes.

This matters in real-world settings where each trial costs something: time, money, or safety. Efficient exploration means reaching good performance in fewer tries, which is the difference between a practical system and an impractical one.

papers.title: EUBRL: Epistemic Uncertainty Directed Bayesian Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Establishes nearly minimax-optimal regret and sample complexity guarantees; demonstrates superior sample efficiency on sparse-reward, long-horizon, stochastic tasks.

papers.title: Lookahead Tree-Based Rollouts for Enhanced Trajectory-Level Exploration in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.contribution: LATR accelerates policy learning by 131% and improves pass@1 performance by 4.2% on GRPO and DAPO across reasoning tasks compared to stochastic sampling.

papers.title: OPRIDE: Efficient Offline Preference-based Reinforcement Learning via In-Dataset Exploration
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms prior methods with substantially fewer queries and achieves strong performance across locomotion, manipulation, and navigation tasks.

papers.title: Queue Length Regret Bounds for Contextual Queueing Bandits
papers.contribution: CQB-ε achieves a regret upper bound of Õ(T^{-1/4}) and CQB-Opt achieves O(log^2 T) for adversarially chosen contexts, validated experimentally.

papers.title: Regret-Guided Search Control for Efficient Learning in AlphaZero
papers.contribution: RGSC improves AlphaZero by 77 Elo on 9×9 Go, 89 Elo on 10×10 Othello, 11×11 Hex; when training on a well-trained 9×9 Go model, increases win rate against KataGo from 69.3% to 78.2%.

papers.title: SHAPO: Sharpness-Aware Policy Optimization for Safe Exploration
papers.contribution: Consistently improves both safety and task performance while significantly expanding Pareto frontiers across continuous-control tasks.

papers.title: Safe Exploration via Policy Priors
papers.contribution: Proves safety guarantees throughout learning and establishes convergence to optimal policy with bounded cumulative regret, validated on safe RL benchmarks and real hardware.

papers.title: Sample-efficient and Scalable Exploration in Continuous-Time RL
papers.contribution: COMBRL achieves sublinear regret in reward-driven setting and provides sample complexity bounds for unsupervised RL, scaling better than prior methods.

papers.title: Tackling Heavy-Tailed Q-Value Bias in Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning with Laplace-Robust Modeling
papers.contribution: LAROO achieves significant performance improvement over baselines by promoting heavy-tailed Q-value biases into a standardized form.

papers.title: Toward Efficient Exploration by Large Language Model Agents
papers.contribution: Demonstrates LLM-based implementation can be more effective than finetuning approaches on natural language tasks requiring prudent exploration.

papers.title: Universal Value-Function Uncertainties
papers.contribution: Achieves ensemble-equivalent performance on challenging offline RL tasks while offering simplicity and substantial computational savings.

papers.title: A Direct Approach for Handling Contextual Bandits with Latent State Dynamics
papers.contribution: Provides high-probability regret bounds depending only on HMM parameter estimation rather than reward functions.

papers.title: A Reward-Free Viewpoint on Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: The approach significantly outperforms state-of-the-art MORL methods across diverse MO-Gymnasium tasks with superior performance and data efficiency while preserving general capabilities.

papers.title: AMPED: Adaptive Multi-objective Projection for balancing Exploration and skill Diversification
papers.contribution: Surpasses SBRL baselines across various benchmarks; theoretical analysis shows greater skill diversity reduces fine-tuning sample complexity.

papers.title: Attention as a Compass: Efficient Exploration for Process-Supervised RL in Reasoning Models
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms prior PSRL approaches on challenging mathematical reasoning benchmarks in terms of performance and sampling/training efficiency.

papers.title: Automating the Refinement of Reinforcement Learning Specifications
papers.contribution: AutoSpec yields improvements in solving more complex control tasks when refined specifications are utilized with RL algorithms.

papers.title: Avoid What You Know: Divergent Trajectory Balance for GFlowNets
papers.contribution: ACE consistently improves approximation accuracy to the target distribution and discovery rate of diverse high-reward states compared to prior curiosity-driven methods.

papers.title: BFTS: Thompson Sampling with Bayesian Additive Regression Trees
papers.contribution: Achieve information-theoretic regret bound of order O-tilde(K sqrt(T)) with competitive empirical results and near-nominal calibration.

papers.title: Best-of-Both-Worlds for Heavy-Tailed Markov Decision Processes
papers.contribution: Achieves Õ(T^1/α) regret in adversarial regimes and O(log T) regret in stochastic regimes for known transitions, with extension to unknown transitions.

papers.title: Beyond Noisy-TVs: Noise-Robust Exploration Via Learning Progress Monitoring
papers.contribution: LPM converges faster, explores more states, and achieves higher extrinsic rewards in noisy environments compared to state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Beyond Static Pipelines: Learning Dynamic Workflows for Text-to-SQL
papers.contribution: Dynamic workflow construction consistently outperforms best static methods, with pronounced gains on complex and out-of-distribution queries.

papers.title: Breaking the Total Variance Barrier: Sharp Sample Complexity for Linear Heteroscedastic Bandits with Fixed Action Set
papers.contribution: VAEE achieves simple regret with a nearly harmonic-mean dependent rate, breaking the total variance barrier and providing a more accurate complexity characterization for heteroscedastic linear bandits.

papers.title: BroRL: Scaling Reinforcement Learning via Broadened Exploration
papers.contribution: Demonstrates continuous performance gains beyond saturation point of ProRL when scaling rollout count.

papers.title: Combinatorial Rising Bandits
papers.contribution: We establish tight regret bounds for the CRB problem and demonstrate effectiveness in deep RL environments and synthetic settings.

papers.title: Contextual Rollout Bandits for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
papers.contribution: Provides theoretical regret bounds and consistent gains in performance and training efficiency across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

papers.title: Contextual Similarity Distillation: Ensemble Uncertainties with a Single Model
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive or superior performance to ensemble baselines on out-of-distribution detection and sparse-reward RL.

papers.title: Covariance Volume Maximization for Embodied Latent Exploration in Deep Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Substantially improves exploration efficiency and robustness on embodied navigation and manipulation tasks, scaling effectively across environments.

papers.title: DF-ExpEnse: Diffusion Filtered Exploration for Sample Efficient Finetuning
papers.contribution: Consistently improves finetuning sample-efficiency across manipulation and locomotion tasks compared to default and alternative baselines.

papers.title: DRIVE: Best Data Scheduling Practices for Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Reward in Competitive Code Generation
papers.contribution: Achieves sota for 32B models in competitive code generation on LeetCode and Codeforces weekly contests; implementation on Qwen2.5-32B and 389B MoE model demonstrates effectiveness and scalability.

papers.title: Demystifying Emergent Exploration in Goal-Conditioned RL
papers.contribution: Exploration dynamics arise from learning low-rank representations rather than function approximation, enabling safety-aware exploration adaptation.

papers.title: Discovering Diverse Behaviors via Temporal Contrastive Learning
papers.contribution: Enables learning of complex exploratory behaviors in locomotion, manipulation, and embodied-AI tasks without extrinsic rewards.

papers.title: Discrete Compositional Generation via General Soft Operators and Robust Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Identifies higher quality, diverse candidates than baselines in synthetic and real-world tasks through robust RL perspective.

papers.title: Diversity-Aware Online Prompt Assignment to Generative Models
papers.contribution: Promotes diversity-aware model selection while maintaining fidelity through two-sample-based expectations over prompt-output pairs.

papers.title: EMFuse: Energy-based Model Fusion for Decision Making
papers.contribution: Provides unified framework for model fusion that avoids computational explosion in ensemble dynamics while balancing exploration and exploitation.

papers.title: Emergence of Exploration in Policy Gradient Reinforcement Learning via Retrying
papers.contribution: Promotes exploration without explicit bonuses on MinAtar and Craftax benchmarks, generalizing discrete retry count to continuous parameter for fine-grained control.

papers.title: Flow Matching with Injected Noise for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves superior performance under limited online budgets on diverse challenging tasks compared to offline-to-online baselines.

papers.title: Geometry of Uncertainty: Learning Metric Spaces for Multimodal State Estimation in RL
papers.contribution: Improved robustness to sensor noise and superior state estimation compared to baselines without explicit noise augmentation.

papers.title: Global Policy-Space Response Oracles for Two-Player Zero-Sum Games
papers.contribution: Achieve lower exploitability and better Nash equilibrium approximation with significantly fewer policy iterations than prior PSRO methods across multiple games.

papers.title: GoldenStart: Q-Guided Priors and Entropy Control for Distilling Flow Policies
papers.contribution: GoldenStart achieves efficient and exploratory policies by designing generative startpoint and controlling entropy; bridges generative models and practical RL.

papers.title: Improved Bounds for Reward-Agnostic and Reward-Free Exploration
papers.contribution: The algorithm significantly relaxes accuracy parameter requirements, achieves minimax sample complexity, and establishes tight lower bounds for reward-free exploration.

papers.title: Incentivized Exploration with Stochastic Covariates: A Two-Stage Mechanism Design for Recommender System
papers.contribution: Algorithm RCB achieves O(sqrt(KdT)) regret while satisfying incentive constraints, and discovers the trade-off between incentive budget and regret.

papers.title: Information-based Value Iteration Networks for Decision Making Under Uncertainty
papers.contribution: Outperforms deep architectures on grid-based navigation tasks and generates interpretable cognitive maps highlighting rewarding and informative locations.

papers.title: Is Pure Exploitation Sufficient in Exogenous MDPs with Linear Function Approximation?
papers.contribution: PEL achieves O(H^2|Xi|√K) regret in tabular case and polynomial regret in continuous spaces, outperforming exploration-based baselines on resource-management tasks.

papers.title: Keep Everyone Happy: Online Fair Division of Numerous Items with Few Copies
papers.contribution: Proposes algorithms for online fair division that achieve provable sub-linear regret without requiring large item copy counts.

papers.title: MOBODY: Model-Based Off-Dynamics Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Outperforms on MuJoCo and Adroit benchmarks by utilizing learned target dynamics to explore high-reward areas inaccessible to existing methods.

papers.title: Meta-RL Induces Exploration in Language Agents
papers.contribution: LaMer improves performance by 11%, 14%, and 19% on Sokoban, MineSweeper, and Webshop respectively, with better generalization to more challenging unseen tasks.

papers.title: Minimax Optimal Adversarial Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Constructs hard MDP instances proving the algorithm is minimax optimal, resolving the fundamental question of achievable regret under adversarial dynamics.

papers.title: Minimax Optimal Strategy for Delayed Observations in Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: Establishes optimal sample complexity for tabular MDPs with delayed observations; general analytical framework applies to MDPs with decomposable transition dynamics.

papers.title: Model-Free Robust Average-Reward Reinforcement Learning with Sample Complexity Analysis
papers.contribution: Achieves ε-optimal robust policy with sample complexity of Õ(SAH²/ε^(2+o(1))) asymptotically matching best robust average-reward RL complexity.

papers.title: Near-Minimax Multi-Objective RL under Predictable Adversarial Preferences and Preference-Free Exploration in Linear MDPs
papers.contribution: Achieves filtration-safe regret bounds with no simplex discretization and matching near-minimax rates in linear MDPs, plus sharp reward-free preference-free exploration guarantees.

papers.title: OGPO: Sample Efficient Full-Finetuning of Generative Control Policies
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art manipulation performance with ability to finetune poorly-initialized BC policies to near task-success using no expert online data and minimal hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Off-Policy Safe Reinforcement Learning with Cost-Constrained Optimistic Exploration
papers.contribution: Achieves high sample efficiency and competitive safety on velocity-constrained locomotion, safe navigation, and autonomous driving with controlled exploration costs.

papers.title: Optimistic Task Inference for Behavior Foundation Models
papers.contribution: OpTI-BFM enables successor-features-based behavior foundation models to identify and optimize unseen reward functions in a handful of episodes.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Reinforcement Learning using Prefix Optimization
papers.contribution: Tuning only the first k tokens significantly improves accuracy, suggesting at least some RLVR gains come from upweighting preferable strategies, delivering substantial gains with tiny compute.

papers.title: Policy Search via Bayesian Optimization with Temporal Difference Gaussian Processes
papers.contribution: Demonstrates practical advantages over baseline methods by exploiting the temporal structure of policy optimization.

papers.title: Posterior Sampling Reinforcement Learning with Gaussian Processes for Continuous Control: Sublinear Regret Bounds for Unbounded State Spaces
papers.contribution: A Bayesian regret bound of O(H*sqrt(gamma_T*T)) resolves prior limitations and provides theoretical foundation for analyzing PSRL in complex settings.

papers.title: Practical and Optimal Algorithm for Linear Contextual Bandits with Rare Parameter Updates
papers.contribution: Achieves minimax-optimal regret (up to polylogarithmic factors) with lowest runtime complexity among optimal algorithms for rare-update contextual bandits.

papers.title: Prior Diffusiveness and Regret in the Linear-Gaussian Bandit
papers.contribution: Establishes that the prior-dependent burn-in term is unavoidable and decouples multiplicatively from long-run regret, contradicting previous bounds.

papers.title: Q-Learning with Fine-Grained Gap-Dependent Regret
papers.contribution: Establishes the first fine-grained gap-dependent regret upper bounds for both UCB and non-UCB methods, with empirical performance improvements.

papers.title: Q-learning with Posterior Sampling
papers.contribution: PSQL achieves a regret bound of O-tilde(H^2*sqrt(SAT)) that closely matches the known lower bound, with novel technical insights for combining posterior sampling with dynamic programming and TD-learning.

papers.title: Reliability-Adjusted Prioritized Experience Replay
papers.contribution: ReaPER outperforms uniform experience replay and PER on diverse environments including classic control and Atari-10 benchmark, matching median Atari-57 score within one percent variance.

papers.title: Rethinking the Hardness of PbRL: A Provable General Regret Bound
papers.contribution: Achieves √T regret with DEED=O(dH) for linear MDPs yielding Õ(dH√T max(H^3/2, 1/κ)) bound, nearly optimal and recovering dueling bandits and standard RL as special cases.

papers.title: Sample Efficient Offline RL via T-Symmetry Enforced Latent State-Stitching
papers.contribution: TELS achieves superior sample efficiency and OOD generalization on D4RL benchmarks and real-world industrial control, significantly outperforming existing offline RL methods on small-sample tasks.

papers.title: Scalable Exploration for High-Dimensional Continuous Control via Value-Guided Flow
papers.contribution: Substantially outperforms online RL baselines and successfully controls a full-body musculoskeletal model for complex movements with superior scalability.

papers.title: Stochastic Linear Bandits with Parameter Noise
papers.contribution: Proves minimax regret is Θ(√(dT σ_q²)) for unit ball action sets and demonstrates attainability via simple explore-exploit algorithm.

papers.title: Taming Aleatoric Impulse in Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning
papers.contribution: DSAC-AID achieves state-of-the-art on Gym-MuJoCo and DeepMind Control Suite by surgically suppressing aleatoric impulse while maintaining exploration.

papers.title: Task-Aware Exploration via a Predictive Bisimulation Metric
papers.contribution: TEB achieves superior exploration ability on MetaWorld and Maze2D, outperforming recent baselines through task-aware novelty measurement.

papers.title: TreePO: Enhancing Policy Efficacy and Inference Efficiency with Tree Modeling
papers.contribution: Reduces GPU hours by 22-43% through computation amortization across prefixes and early pruning, achieves up to 40% trajectory-level and 35% token-level sampling compute reduction while enhancing exploration.

papers.title: Unsupervised Learning of Efficient Exploration: Pre-training Adaptive Policies via Self-Imposed Goals
papers.contribution: ULEE pre-training yields improved exploration and adaptation that generalizes to novel objectives, environment dynamics, and map structures.

papers.title: Value Aggregation with Uncertainty in Online Decentralized MARL
papers.contribution: Establishes theoretical guarantees on accelerated convergence and bounded learning variance, advancing MARL theory.

papers.title: Variance Driven Exploration: A Provable and Efficient Methodology for Pure Exploration in Highly Stochastic Environments
papers.contribution: Demonstrates consistent and significant improvements over existing methods in Best Arm Identification, Monte Carlo Tree Search, and Best-Policy Identification with theoretical guarantees on variance decay.

papers.title: XRPO: Pushing the Limits of GRPO with Targeted Exploration and Exploitation
papers.contribution: Outperforms GRPO by up to 4% pass@1 on math and coding benchmarks while accelerating convergence up to 2.7x.
